Company Overview
Swarm Defense Technologies designs and builds small unmanned aircraft systems for the U.S. Department of Defense. We are headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, where electrical design, firmware, machining, assembly, and flight test all happen under one roof. Our current work is focused on moving production-ready small UAS from prototype to volume delivery on compressed program timelines, and we are building the engineering and manufacturing team to do it.
Job Summary
Swarm Defense is hiring a UAS Engineer who has spent years designing, building, and flying drones and wants to do it for a living on aircraft that get fielded. This is a generalist role. On a given week you might be laying out a new airframe, integrating a flight controller and payload, tuning a control loop, building a test article, or standing on the flight line running the test card and diagnosing why the aircraft did not do what it was supposed to. If you have built and flown your own aircraft, crashed them, figured out why, and built them better, that is the background we are looking for. We care more about what you have flown than what is on your resume.
You will join a small engineering team where the same people design, build, and fly the aircraft, and you will own a piece of the aircraft end to end. You will work directly with our mechanical, electrical, and embedded engineers and with the production floor. Our design-to-flight cycle is measured in weeks, not quarters.
Key Responsibilities
Design and integrate small UAS subsystems: airframe, propulsion, power, flight controller, sensors, payload, and communication links.
Build prototype and test aircraft by hand, from initial bring-up through flight-ready configuration.
Plan and execute flight tests: write test cards, fly or direct flights, capture data, and turn results into design changes.
Configure and tune flight control stacks (PX4, ArduPilot, or similar), including parameter tuning, failsafes, and mission behavior.
Diagnose flight anomalies from logs, telemetry, and hardware inspection; run root cause to closure.
Select and qualify components (motors, ESCs, props, batteries, radios, sensors) against performance and reliability requirements.
Produce the drawings, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and build instructions needed for production to build what you tested.
Maintain the aircraft fleet, ground control equipment, and test infrastructure so testing is never blocked on hardware.
Follow and improve flight safety procedures and range operations for testing.
Requirements
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and flying multirotor or fixed-wing UAS, professional or personal. You must be able to show us aircraft you have built and explain the design decisions.
Hands-on with the full small-UAS stack: airframe, motors/ESCs, power systems, flight controllers, radios, and GPS/IMU sensors.
Working knowledge of PX4, ArduPilot, Betaflight, or comparable flight control firmware, including configuration and log analysis.
Competent with common build tools and methods: soldering, crimping, basic machining or 3D printing, CAD.
Able to methodically troubleshoot a system that spans mechanical, electrical, and software domains.
BS in aerospace, mechanical, electrical engineering or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
Bonus Points
FAA Part 107 certificate and real flight hours on aircraft you built.
Experience with UAS at 5 kg or above, fixed-wing or VTOL platforms, or autonomous mission flight.
Ability to read and modify flight controller firmware or write ground-side tooling (C/C++, Python).
Experience with RF systems, video links, or mesh radios.
Competitive or club drone experience (racing, freestyle, long-range, or university UAS teams).
Defense, aerospace, or other regulated hardware environment.
Prior exposure to flight testing under a written test plan and safety review.
Benefits
Health Insurance: We cover 100% of health insurance premiums for our employees.
401(k): Company retirement plan with employer match.
﻿
Swarm Defense is an early-stage defense company, and the pace is set by what the mission requires. The work is hands-on: engineers build what they design, test it on real aircraft, and own the result. Timelines are short, feedback from the field is direct, and problems get solved by the people closest to them.
We reward initiative and give people ownership of their area. If you want to see your work fly within weeks rather than years, and you are comfortable operating without a large support structure around you, this is the right environment.

Hands-on experience with CI/CD, dependency/build systems, and infrastructure-as-code.
End-to-end observability experience: logging, metrics, tracing.
Docker/Kubernetes; release management, phased rollouts, and operational readiness for controlled networks.

Experience with DAQ and closed-loop control (lab/test control environments).
Prior work on CI/testing/simulation/data tools integrated with flight software teams.

Knowledge of ground systems standards; security in mission networks.
Experience building mission-grade UIs with structured command workflows, alarming, and situational awareness.

About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
The
Systems Engineer II, Avionics
oversees the design, integration, and testing of avionics systems for our Winnebago Spaceship. They ensure that all systems are ready for both launch and operational phases, requiring a deep understanding of avionics system design, manufacturing processes, and operational protocols. They closely collaborate with various engineering teams and navigate conflicting requirements to achieve seamless system integration. Their expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry.
Responsibilities
Collaborate with cross functional teams to define project scopes and initial requirements, guiding designs from concept to prototype and full-scale production.
Develop electrical architecture, system diagrams, and budgets to account for power, telemetry, channel count, size, and mass predictions used to communicate closing vehicle solutions to company level objectives.
Analyze architecture for potential faults and risks, develop comprehensive mitigation plans, resolve uncertainties, and collaborate on Fault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) or operational workarounds when hardware solutions are unfeasible.
Conduct comprehensive verification plans for avionics systems on flight and HITL hardware, ensuring readiness for launch and compliance with mission objectives for space and reentry operations.
Participate in mission operations as an Avionics specialist or system operator, where they’ll determine system health, suggest corrective actions to reentry commit criteria for operational success.
Oversee the integration of the Winnebago avionics systems, acting as the primary point of contact for integrated systems investigations.
Design, build, and operate the Hardware In The Loop (HITL) testbeds, simulating the spacecraft on the ground to ensure all systems are mission ready.
Develop avionics ground infrastructure, support the design and integration of test racks and R&D equipment used to power and communicate with the flight vehicles. Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.
Draw from their experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.
Basic Qualifications
Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field.
Experience: 3+ years of experience in system design, test planning, and validation.
Programming Skills: Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.
Technical Expertise: Experience with power supplies, modular DAQ systems, RTD and 4-20mA devices, and general test equipment.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Proven experience taking vehicle electrical systems from concept to operational production.
Prior experience setting up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and conducting system level tests.
Familiarity with Unix environments and the ability to use command line utilities.
Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.
Strong project or program management skills.
Relevant prior roles: Avionics Hardware, FPGA Engineer, Electronics Test Engineer, Electrical Systems Engineer
Pay Range
Salary range: Engineer II: $119,543 - $152,749/ per year.
This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA.
Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance.
You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards
Benefits
Consider your benefits covered for launch.
At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.
Regular Full-Time Positions:
Health & Wellness
Flexible PTO policy + 12 paid holidays
100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options
Voluntary accident, hospital, critical illness, and pet insurance
$120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses
12 weeks of parental leave (with supplemental disability leave for CA mothers)
Family building, pregnancy, parenting and menopause benefits via Maven Clinic
Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents

Forward Deployed Engineers sit between our customers and our codebase. Some days you'll be in a working session with a compliance team learning how they actually run an alert to disposition; other days you'll be in our repos shipping the pipeline that makes that workflow ten times faster.
Roughly half of this job is building the core product alongside the rest of engineering. The other half is deploying, extending, and tuning it inside real customer environments. This is not a support or solutions role, you'll be held to the same engineering bar as everyone else on the team. The difference is that you will be the engineer that customers go to first, and the one who sees their problems firsthand.
What You'll Do
Build

Bridge the current platform to customers with custom connectors, enrichment steps, migration scripts, internal tooling, etc
Be the credible technical voice in the room, whether you're talking to an analyst who has never seen an API or to their staff engineer who is skeptical of yours
Close the loop
Distinguish one-offs from the emerging pattern, and push patterns back into the core platform
Bring the field back to engineering, product, and leadership as evidence for what to prioritize
Set honest expectations with customers about what's shipping and when, and hold the line when the answer is "not soon"
Leave behind runbooks, docs, and internal write-ups so the next deployment is faster than the last

Job Summary
We are seeking Software Engineers – AI Automation (Internal Tools) to join Voyager’s Internal Tools Team. In this role, you will help design and build AI-driven automations, bots, and internal applications that streamline how Voyager runs—from finance and HR to supply chain, manufacturing, and business development.
You will work closely with the Internal AI Tools Lead and business stakeholders to understand real-world pain points, then turn them into concrete, working systems. You will build integrations, write services, wire up LLMs and agents, and ship tools that remove repetitive work from the organization and make our teams faster, more accurate, and more focused on high-value tasks.
This role is ideal for early-career engineers (including exceptional new graduates) who love building things, are comfortable talking to users, and are excited to use AI as a core part of their engineering toolkit.
You will be joining the Internal AI Tools Team, a small, high-leverage engineering group focused on building AI-powered systems that run Voyager itself. This team designs and delivers internal platforms, automations, and copilots that turn slow, manual workflows into streamlined, integrated systems.
We work across the entire business—Finance & Accounting, Internal Communications, Performance Management, Human Resources, IT & Infrastructure, Cyber Security & Systems Assurance, Mergers & Acquisitions, R&D and Technology Roadmapping, Strategic Planning, Enterprise Risk Management, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain & Procurement, Manufacturing & Assembly, and Sales / New Business Capture.
Our goal is simple: multiply the effectiveness of every team at Voyager by replacing spreadsheet-driven, email-based processes with secure, AI-driven workflows, decision-support tools, and intelligent assistants that dramatically reduce cycle times and improve execution quality.
Responsibilities
Build and maintain AI-powered automations and workflows that streamline recurring business processes (e.g., report generation, approval flows, policy Q&A, data reconciliation).
Implement internal tools and microservices that integrate with systems across Finance & Accounting, HR, IT, Cyber Security, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Sales / New Business Capture.
Develop and maintain Slack/Teams bots, web frontends, and small internal apps that serve as “copilots” for business users.
Use LLMs and agent frameworks to design task-specific assistants—such as a contract summarization agent, a supplier risk analysis agent, or an internal policy advisor bot.
Work with the Internal AI Tools Lead and business stakeholders to map manual workflows into clear technical requirements and automation designs.
Leverage agentic to rapidly write clean, tested code and contribute to shared libraries, templates, and best practices for internal automations.
Monitor and debug automations in production; improve reliability and performance based on real-world usage and feedback.
Required Qualifications
0–3 years of professional software engineering experience (internships, research, or substantial personal projects all count; exceptional new graduates are encouraged to apply).
Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar.
Experience building scripts, APIs, small web apps, or workflow automations—whether in a professional setting, research lab, or serious side projects.

About Us
Culture’s mission is to simplify and accelerate bioprocess development to enable our customers to bring their biopharmaceutical products to market faster.
With a focus on upstream cell culture process development, Culture has developed a unique platform that merges products, services and data management that can be applied to mammalian, microbial and viral vector production processes. This platform enables high-throughput process development projects to be rapidly and seamlessly executed directly by our customers in their own facilities, in our service laboratories, or both, all driven by our cloud-connected web application, accessible from anywhere, for designing, managing and analyzing experiments.
At Culture, we combine our passions for biomanufacturing, engineering, and operations to build new solutions that make bioprocess development faster. We value curiosity, communication, collaboration, a customer focused mindset and a drive for results.
The Opportunity
We're looking for a Software Engineer who has experience in automation and controls to design, build, and maintain automation systems for our Bioreactor and Bioprocessing business. This person is comfortable with physical systems, has a deep understanding of control loop
theory, and comes with a strong focus in controls, closed-loop system behavior, and PID-based control strategies. When a temperature control starts to oscillate, you can dive in, look at the traces, have a working theory of where the feedback loop went wrong, and come up with
solutions to compensate and add margin to the design.
The role is more than just PID tuning. You will own everything from the interface of our Cloud software through the low-level control of a physical device (from Ethernet to USB). This role will work across software, hardware, and systems teams to develop reliable automation solutions
for complex physical systems, improve process performance, and enable scalable, repeatable operation. Our software controls physical processes that run for days at a time, where failures can ruin an expensive experiment.
What You’ll Do
Tune and troubleshoot control loops in real-world environments, including diagnosing oscillation, lag, overshoot, and instability. Improve automation reliability through monitoring, logging, fault detection, and recovery mechanisms.
Evolve our AsyncAPI hardware interface so higher-level automation and AI systems can safely interact with physical equipment, with explicit permissions, validation, and fail-safe behavior.

Description
As part of the AWS Applied AI Solutions organization, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers’ businesses through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions that solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon’s real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.
Humorphic Labs builds AI systems that work as teammates rather than tools, and ships them six months or more ahead of anyone else. The Lab is small on purpose, so it can change direction in a day.
Humorphism is the quality of the working relationship between a person and an AI system. It asks whether the system acts proactively, adapts to the person and the situation, earns trust, manages attention, and strengthens human judgment. The work is closing the distance between a tool a person operates and a teammate a person collaborates with.
You will start in the Lab and build a capability that does not exist yet. Then you will deploy into the Applied AI Solutions product team that carries it, and stay until that product ships it and customers use it. Adoption is yours. Over time the same pattern extends to AWS service teams.
The Lab does not run production at scale. Once a capability proves itself, architecture and scaling move to the product team, and you return with what you learned.
There is no fixed technology stack. The work leans toward the web frontend, because a teammate is judged on the surface where a person meets it, and extends to native mobile, voice, and other modalities as the problem demands. Some of these problems have no known solution today. Multimodality is one.
The Lab is a lead who still writes code, an Applied Scientist, and engineers. Applied AI Solutions leadership approved it with one instruction — to explore the limits of what we can build — and one number: to ship six or more months ahead of what others can do.
The Applied Scientist owns the hypotheses and the evaluation. You build the systems that test them and the products that carry the ones that survive.
We have a sunset clause. Once a capability is proven and integrated into its product, the Lab moves to the next frontier.
Key job responsibilities
Build AI teammate capabilities in the Lab, from a thesis to a working product, in line with the Humorphism design philosophy and with guidance from the Lab lead and the Applied Scientist.
Implement the experiments the Applied Scientist designs, and turn research results into working software.
Deploy into a product team, work alongside them, and drive your capability into their product.
Own adoption of what you build. Measure it, report it, and stay until customers use it.
Identify where the work breaks down in a host team's hands, then correct the cause rather than the symptom.
Partner with UX designers, product teams, and other organizations to deliver complete humorphic experiences.
Transfer architecture and scaling to the product team at the agreed boundary, with the documentation and tests that make the transfer safe.
Contribute your work back into the shared humorphic layer, so the next capability starts from a higher floor.
Learn unfamiliar languages, runtimes, and problem domains as the work requires.
Write tested code, review the code of others, and operate what the Lab runs.
Present the work to the host team, the Lab, and SCORE, and participate in internal reviews.
A day in the life
Your calendar has two shapes.
In a Lab week you write code most of the day. You take a thesis about how a teammate should behave, build the smallest version that tests it, and put it in front of a person before the week ends. You sit with a UX designer to work out how the behavior should feel, not only what it does.
In a deployed week you sit with the product team carrying your capability. You watch a real user hit the seam between your work and theirs, and you fix it that afternoon. Expect occasional travel.

This is a hands-on engineering role at the customer edge.
Not a ticket queue.
Not an account manager reading from a script.
Not a note-taker on customer calls.
You unblock customers by writing code that helps them integrate, run customized demos, and get thier solution to production.
Credence ID builds digital identity products that run in the real world — mobile ID (mDL) verification, biometric hardware, and the SDKs behind them. Our customers are government agencies, enterprises, stadiums, and airports. When one of them starts an evaluation, somebody technical has to take them from “this looks interesting” to a working integration in production. That somebody is you.
You'll be the first engineer most customers meet. During evals and pilots you'll build the proof-of-concept, wire up the API and SDK integrations, run the demos, and chase down whatever breaks. Once they buy, you stay on through deployment.
What You'll Actually Do
•     Own the technical side of customer evaluations — demos, onboarding, pilots, and the path to production
•     Build POCs, sample apps, and integration scripts against our APIs, SDKs, and hardware (Android is a big part of our world)
•     Turn vague customer requirements into working prototypes, fast
•     Reproduce and troubleshoot customer-reported issues, then drive them to resolution with Engineering and QA
•     Run technical training and demos for customer teams
•     Team up with Sales and pre-sales on solution proposals, technical inquiries, and RFP/RFI responses — you write the parts that have to be technically right
•     Feed what you learn in the field back to Product and Sales — you'll see problems before anyone else does
•     Use AI coding tools daily to prototype, test, debug, and document faster
What We Care About (Read This Carefully)
You can build.
Degree in CS, EE, CE, or similar, and 0–3 years of experience — a strong fresh grad with real projects beats five years of watching other people code. Show us something you built: a repo, an app, a hardware hack, a class project you took further than the assignment required.
You can talk to people.
You'll be in front of customers from week one — explaining, demoing, and sometimes saying “I don't know yet, let me find out.” Clear writing and clear speaking are not optional here.
You debug like it's a sport.
A customer says “it doesn't work.” You figure out what “it” is, reproduce the failure, isolate the cause, and don't let go until it's fixed.
You're AI-native.
You use Claude, Copilot, or similar tools every day and can show us how they make you faster — not “I tried ChatGPT once.”
You take ownership.
Small company. Nobody hands you a runbook. If a customer is stuck, it's your problem until it isn't.
Nice to Have
Exposure to digital identity, mDL, mobile wallets, NFC, BLE, QR/PDF417, biometrics, or PKI. None of it is required — we'll teach the domain. We can't teach curiosity.
What This Role Is (and Isn't)
It
is
a 3-month contract first. That's deliberate — you see how we work, we see how you work, and if it fits, you convert to full-time.
It
is
a launchpad. Do this well and the paths open up: solutions architecture, product, or core engineering.
It
isn't
a pure coding job. Half your week is customer-facing. If you want to sit behind a compiler with headphones on, this isn't your seat.
It
isn't
scripted. Every customer integration is different — different stack, different constraints, different surprises.
Culture Notes
We're a small, fast-moving team. People get responsibility early and are expected to run with it. We value people who understand the customer, get hands-on with the technology, build quickly, and test their own work before someone else has to.
How to Apply
Send a short note about the most interesting thing you've built and why, plus a link to it if one exists. No AI-written replies — we'll know, and it defeats the purpose of hiring someone who can communicate.

We Are:
Accenture LearnVantage helps organizations transform how their people learn and work. We partner with enterprise clients to design and deliver high-quality, scalable, outcome-driven learning that builds the skills their workforces need. Udacity, now part of Accenture LearnVantage, brings deep expertise in technical upskilling through hands-on, project-based online learning. Together we build learning experiences that help people gain in-demand skills in cloud, data, AI, and more.
You Are:
You are a technical learning content developer who turns cloud expertise into learning experiences that stick. You combine hands-on cloud knowledge with a grounding in how adults learn, and you care that learners can demonstrably apply a skill in a real-world setting, not just consume content. You own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you build, you use AI tooling to work faster without dropping the quality bar, and you collaborate well with subject matter experts, authors, and testers. You move toward solutions even when requirements are ambiguous, guided by data but biased toward action.
The Work:
Join the Learning Experience team and help build the cloud learning experiences that power effective workforce upskilling at enterprise scale. As a Technical Content Developer, you'll take design requirements and learning objectives from the pod roadmap and partner with subject matter experts to build course modules, hands-on labs, projects, and assessments. You'll own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you produce so that learners can demonstrably apply new cloud skills on the job.
Develop technical learning experiences (courses, modules, hands-on labs, projects, quizzes, and assessments) against defined design requirements and learning objectives for the cloud domain.
Translate design requirements into learning experiences that lead to verifiable skill acquisition and application, not just content consumption.
Author and test hands-on labs and projects end to end, making sure cloud environments are configured correctly and working solutions are reproducible by every learner.
Build assessments, quizzes, and other instructional-design elements that measure whether the target skill was actually acquired, in line with LearnVantage learning standards.
Validate the technical accuracy of all content, partnering with subject matter experts and authors to keep pace with changes in cloud platforms and tools.
Use AI tooling to accelerate drafting, iteration, and QA of content, raising throughput without sacrificing quality.
Incorporate feedback from testers, learners, and reviewers into content revisions.
In this role, you'll work in a curriculum pod and report into a Curriculum Lead.
What's In It for You?
You'll build cloud learning that reaches people at enterprise scale and gives them skills they can apply on the job, not just content they consume.
You'll work at the leading edge of AI-accelerated content development, helping shape the tooling and workflows the pipeline depends on.
Accenture will continually invest in your craft and growth, with access to certifications, learning resources, and a global community of practitioners.
You'll collaborate with subject matter experts, authors, and testers across Accenture LearnVantage and Udacity.
Here's What You Need:
Minimum 2 years of deep hands-on cloud expertise across at least one major platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), with an emphasis on how enterprise teams apply cloud skills in their roles.
Minimum 2 years of experience in instructional design, grounded in adult learning science (scaffolding, retrieval practice, cognitive load, and assessment).
Minimum 1 year of experience authoring and testing hands-on labs and projects end-to-end, including environment troubleshooting.
Minimum 1 year of experience with AI tooling for drafting, iteration, and QA.
Minimum 2 years of experience in Cloud Computing and AI Prompting.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in instructional design or curriculum development.
Minimum 2 years in a cloud-related role (Solutions Architect, Cloud Architect, Cloud Engineer, or Data Architect).
Minimum 1 year of experience with version control tools like Git.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

The Opportunity
insitro is a physical AI company dedicated to unlocking causal human biology and accelerating the delivery of better medicines to patients. Our unique Virtual Human™ platform identifies novel, high-impact genetic intervention points, which our TherML™ platform translates into therapeutics—whether small molecules, biologics, or oligos. With multiple programs in metabolic disease and neuroscience advancing toward the clinic, and our first IND submission slated for the second half of this year, we are at a pivotal inflection point.
To enable that mission, we need a software layer that ties together the scientific, automation, and machine learning platforms — that's our Lab Platform: a harness for science, built as an agentic workflow system that lets scientists drive the lab through an agent. Our bar is that everything in the lab should be agentically accessible (any action a scientist can take, an agent can take), agentically legible (agents understand what the data means in insitro's context, not just how to fetch it), and humanly verifiable (a scientist can always check what an agent did and why). This is real robotics, workflow automation, and applied agent tooling — and your users are in the building with you.

Full-Stack Ownership
Ship Across the Stack: Build the React and TypeScript frontends scientists use every day, the Python services behind them, and integrations that reach instruments, Benchling, and agent runtimes
Own It End to End: Take a feature from the first conversation with a scientist through the data model and UI to the alert that fires when it breaks

Agentic Tooling & Experimentation

Figure Out What's Actually Useful: Test agentic tooling ideas through prototypes, real users, and short iterative loops rather than betting on theory
Move the Needle: Contribute work that meaningfully advances insitro's mission and the pace of drug development
Cross-Functional Partnership
Go Watch the Work: Spend time in the lab observing the workflow before you change it
Partner Broadly: Collaborate closely with machine learning, automation, and biology teams to build tools people actually use
Keep Humans in the Loop: Design for provenance and verifiability, so a scientist can always check what an agent did and why

Engineering Fundamentals: Working knowledge of AWS or GCP, relational databases, and standard practices like version control and code review

Product Instinct: You think like a product person — you want to know who the user is, what they're actually trying to do, and you have opinions about what to build
Curious About the Science: You don't need a biology background, but you want to learn the domain rather than treat it as someone else's problem
Comfortable in the Gray Area: You can reason clearly about the tradeoffs between quality and speed
Fits the Team: You're up for writing design docs, having opinions in code review, and yes, goofing around on Slack.

Domain Experience: Experience with LIMS, lab automation, or another life sciences domain

The FDE team supports Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC) and Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) to monitor and assess the current performance and accuracy of the Minuteman III ICBM. Cowboy Space Corporation is transforming how civilization powers, computes and connects - from orbit to Earth.
Background
Cowboy Space Corporation is building the infrastructure to power and connect the orbital economy. Our modular, scalable satellites collect sunlight in Low Earth Orbit to enable multiple integrated applications: transmitting energy via infrared lasers (space-to-earth and space-to-space), powering on-orbit high-performance computing clusters (GPU/TPU), and providing secure, high bandwidth optical data transport.
Current energy and data systems rely on complex logistics and outdated infrastructure. Cowboy Space Corporation overcomes these challenges by enabling direct, on-demand, secure, and scalable energy distribution and data processing from space. This will revolutionize how we operate in orbit and on Earth, supporting the rapidly expanding space industrial base, ISAM (In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing) operations, remote regions, and military bases.
Baiju Bhatt founded Cowboy Space Corporation in 2024. This is an ambitious mission that demands extraordinary talent. Job Description
About the Team
Our Mapping organization is building national-scale, next-generation mapping systems that move beyond static HD maps toward automated, algorithmic and ML-assisted map reconstruction pipelines powered by onboard sensor data. These systems form a critical foundation for localization, perception, simulation, and autonomy at scale.
The Role
We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to design and build the mapping algorithms and geospatial data systems behind automated map reconstruction and maintenance within our Mapping Engineering team.
In this role, you will develop the algorithms and data models that reconstruct, conflate, validate, and maintain map primitives — lanes, lane connectivity, road network graphs, boundaries, traffic controls, and signs — from large-scale multi-modal sensor data. You will own the geometric and topological correctness of the map itself: how features are represented, how disparate sources are merged, and how errors are detected before they reach the vehicle.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role with strong ownership. You will drive technical problems end to end, partner closely with Perception, Localization, and Simulation, and apply machine learning where it measurably improves accuracy, coverage, or automation rate.
What You'll Do (Responsibilities)
Design and implement mapping algorithms for map reconstruction and maintenance — lane and boundary extraction, road network graph construction, map conflation and matching, geometry simplification, and topology validation.
Build and evolve geospatial data models for lane-level connectivity at intersections, road network graphs, and associated map attributes and restrictions.
Develop large-scale distributed geospatial pipelines that process sensor-derived and third-party road data into production map releases on a recurring cadence.
Apply machine learning and computer vision models — detection, segmentation, 3D reconstruction, BEV representations — to automate feature extraction and map change detection, and integrate them into production pipelines.
Build automated quality, validation, and regression systems that catch geometric, topological, and semantic map defects before release, with clear accuracy metrics.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Perception, Localization, Simulation, and Platform teams on interfaces, data contracts, and integration points.
Diagnose and resolve system-level issues spanning geospatial data pipelines, algorithms, models, and production workflows.
Contribute to design reviews, engineering best practices, and mentorship of engineers on the team.
Minimum Qualifications (Must-Have)
3+ years of software engineering experience building production systems, with a substantial portion focused on mapping, geospatial, or geometric algorithms.
Strong applied foundation in geospatial and computational geometry concepts — coordinate systems and projections, spatial indexing, geometry operations, map matching, and graph algorithms on road networks.
Demonstrated experience designing geospatial data models and working with road network or map data structures (lanes, segments, intersections, topology).
Hands-on experience with machine learning or computer vision workflow in production — dataset curation, model training or fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment.
Experience building large-scale distributed data pipelines for geospatial or sensor data.
Proficiency in Python and C++.
BS or MS in Computer Science, GIS, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent industry experience.
Ability to own ambiguous, well-scoped technical problems end to end and drive them to production.
Preferred Qualifications (nice To Have)
Experience with HD maps, localization, perception, or robotics systems, particularly in autonomous driving or mobile robotics.
Hands-on experience with 3D geometry, multi-view geometry, point cloud processing, or SLAM.
Familiarity with AV sensor data (camera, lidar, radar) and real-world data challenges such as noise, drift, and long-tail scenarios.
Experience with map conflation, change detection, or automated map QA at national or global scale.
Experience with geospatial tooling and formats (PostGIS, GeoPandas, GDAL/OGR, S2/H3, OSM, GeoJSON).
Experience deploying ML models into production pipelines with monitoring, validation, and iteration loops.
Experience mentoring engineers or acting as a technical lead on a project.
3+ years of software engineering experience building production systems, with a substantial portion focused on mapping, geospatial, or geometric algorithms.
